summary: My declared family (residual-stream topology) was a dead end and I killed it early: U-Net encoder->decoder skips with learned zero-init gates measured 1.001559 vs the 0.997333 baseline, and value embeddings on all 8 layers instead of the alternating 4 measured 0.985629 vs 0.984898 on an identical config (a peer replicated that at 0.985588). What did work was capacity and attention locality at the batch size the whole cell converged on: my best run db469bb (0.977649) is depth 8 / dim 768 / MLP 4x / HEAD_DIM 128 / TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 / DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 / WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7 with the six 'S' layers attending over seq/16 (128 tokens). I contributed the combination runs (fe7e420 0.979108 was the leader when posted) and the single-variable window sweep that brackets the optimum: seq/4 -> seq/8 -> seq/16 each improved, seq/32 regressed to 0.978546. Next I would retune the Muon/Adam LRs at this new shape (LRs x1.3 was measured worse on an older shape but was never re-tested at dim 768 with short windows), test MLP_RATIO 4->5 at dim 768, and revisit depth 9 at width 768 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -- depth increases were only ever tested at device batch 64, which alone costs ~0.008 and so confounded every depth result in this cell.
